outcomes.source: demo:Everyday English A2 / Lesson 1: Hello and introductions
outcomes.criterion: Uses the right greeting for the time of day
outcomes.skill: Choose the greeting that matches the time of day
outcomes.belief: "Good morning" is the polite greeting at any time of day.

pre.prompt: It is 7 pm. You meet your neighbour. What do you say? "Good ___!"
It is 2 pm. You meet your teacher. What do you say? "Good ___!"

post.prompt: It is 8 o'clock at night. You see a friend. "Good ___!"
It is 3 o'clock in the afternoon. You enter an office. "Good ___!"

transfer.prompt: You start a phone call at 6:30 pm with a hotel. Write your first two words.
You write an email that will be read at 1 pm. Begin it with a greeting for that time. "Good ___"

ret1.prompt: It is 9 pm at a family dinner. Greet your uncle: "Good ___!"
It is 4 pm. Greet the shop owner: "Good ___!"

ret2.prompt: It is 5 pm and the sun is still up. Greet a visitor: "Good ___!"
It is 10 pm at a party. Greet the host: "Good ___!"

outcomes.criterion: Says "This is … He/She is a …" correctly
outcomes.skill: Introduce someone and say their job with This is … / He/She is a …
outcomes.belief: When I say someone's job, I leave out "a": "She is doctor."

pre.prompt: Complete: "This is Ali. He is ___ (teacher)."
Complete: "This is Sara. She is ___ (nurse)."

post.prompt: Complete: "This is Omar. He is ___ (pilot)."
Complete: "This is Huda. She is ___ (student)."

transfer.prompt: Write one sentence about your friend Karim, who is an engineer, starting "He is".
Introduce your aunt, a farmer, in one sentence starting "She is".

ret1.prompt: Complete: "This is Ziad. He is ___ (driver)."
Complete: "This is Laila. She is ___ (chef)."

ret2.prompt: Complete: "This is Nabil. He is ___ (artist)."
Complete: "This is Reem. She is ___ (singer)."

outcomes.source: demo:Lesson 2: My daily routine; fixture v2 A2 My daily routine
outcomes.skill: Add -s/-es to the verb after he/she/it in the present simple
outcomes.belief: The verb is the same for all people: "she go", "he watch".

pre.prompt: Correct the verb: "My brother play football on Fridays." Write the correct verb.
Correct the verb: "She watch TV every evening." Write the correct verb.

post.prompt: Correct the verb: "My father drive to work." Write the correct verb.

Correct the verb: "He catch the bus at 7." Write the correct verb.

ret2.prompt: Complete: "The baby ___ (cry) at night."
Complete: "My mum ___ (teach) maths."

outcomes.criterion: Puts always/usually/sometimes/never before the main verb
outcomes.skill: Place adverbs of frequency before the main verb
outcomes.belief: Frequency words go at the end of the sentence: "I eat breakfast always."

pre.prompt: Put the words in order: "I / always / breakfast / eat".
Put the words in order: "She / never / coffee / drinks".

post.prompt: Put the words in order: "We / usually / walk / to school".

accepted: my grandmother always drinks tea at 5

ret1.prompt: Put the words in order: "They / often / visit / us".
Put the words in order: "I / usually / read / at night".

ret2.prompt: Put the words in order: "She / always / smiles".
Put the words in order: "We / never / watch / horror films".

outcomes.criterion: Uses "Can I have …, please?" or "I'd like …"

outcomes.skill: Form the present perfect for life experiences
outcomes.belief: For experiences I use have + the past simple form: "I have saw", "she has went".

profiles.name: Beginner with large gaps
profiles.language: very limited English (A1 words, short incomplete sentences)
profiles.accuracy: often wrong; unsure of basic words
profiles.errors: wrong word order, missing verbs, wrong forms
profiles.text: You are a beginner with big gaps. You know very little of this topic beyond the prerequisite. You change your belief only after a clear, simple explanation that you can follow, and often need it repeated.

profiles.name: Partial understanding
profiles.errors: applies the rule in part of the cases but not in others
profiles.text: You partly understand this topic: about half the time you apply the correct pattern, the other half you fall back on your belief.

profiles.name: Strong foundations
profiles.text: You already understand this topic well and usually answer correctly. You do not hold the belief below as your own; it is a mistake you know other learners make.

profiles.name: Persistent misconception
profiles.accuracy: consistently wrong in the same way
profiles.hints: hints alone rarely change the belief
profiles.text: You hold your belief very firmly. You keep applying it even after hints. You only change it if the teaching names your mistaken idea directly and explains why it is wrong with clear examples; even then you may slip back.

profiles.name: Careless
profiles.accuracy: knows more than it shows; about 1 in 4 answers has a careless slip
profiles.errors: typos, missing letters, skipped words, rushing
profiles.text: You often understand but rush: in about one answer out of four you make a careless slip (a typo, a missing letter, a skipped word) even when you know the rule.

profiles.name: Limited English proficiency
profiles.language: very limited English; struggles to understand long explanations
profiles.errors: misreads instructions, answers a different question
profiles.text: Your English reading is weak: long or complex explanations confuse you and you understand only short, simple sentences with examples. If the explanation is long or in hard English, you do not learn from it.

profiles.name: Understands but struggles to express
profiles.errors: incomplete sentences, wrong word in a correct structure
profiles.text: You often understand the idea but find it hard to write the answer: your answers are short and sometimes incomplete, even when you know the rule.

profiles.name: Fast learner
profiles.text: You start with the belief below but you learn quickly: one clear explanation with an example is usually enough for you to change it.

profiles.name: Needs repeated scaffolding
profiles.errors: gets one part right, misses another
profiles.text: You need small steps and several practice turns before a new rule sticks; a single explanation is not enough for you.

profiles.name: Guesser
profiles.speed: fast to answer, slow to learn
profiles.errors: random choices, copies words from the question
profiles.text: You do not think much: you answer quickly by guessing, often copying words from the question, and you would rather be told the answer than work it out.

demo1.title: Lesson 1: Hello and introductions
demo1.objective: Greet people and introduce yourself and others.

objectives: Introduce a friend and say their job
successCriteria: Uses the right greeting for the time of day
Says "This is … He/She is a …" correctly
examples: Hello, I'm Lina. Nice to meet you.
This is Mona. She is a doctor.

successCriteria: Uses "Can I have …, please?" or "I'd like …"
Uses a/an with countable and some with uncountable nouns
examples: Can I have a coffee, please?

demo4.title: Lesson 4: Last weekend
demo4.objective: Talk about finished actions in the past.

objectives: Talk about finished actions in the past
successCriteria: Uses went, had, saw, ate correctly
examples: What did you do last weekend?

fx_a1.title: Talking about my family
fx_a1.objective: Introduce family members using "This is my …" and "He is / She is …".

objectives: Introduce a family member with "This is my …"
Say one fact about them with "He is / She is …"
successCriteria: Uses "This is my + family word" correctly
examples: This is my sister. She is ten.
This is my father. He is a driver.

fx_a2.title: My daily routine
fx_a2.objective: Describe daily routines with the present simple, including he/she/it + -s and adverbs of frequency.

objectives: Describe a routine with the present simple
Place adverbs of frequency before the main verb
successCriteria: Puts always/usually/sometimes/never before the main verb
grammar: adverbs of frequency before the main verb
examples: My brother usually gets up at seven.
I never have coffee in the evening.

fx_b1.title: Life experiences
fx_b1.objective: Talk about life experiences with the present perfect and contrast it with the past simple for finished times.

objectives: Use the past simple, not the present perfect, with a finished time (yesterday, last year)
successCriteria: Switches to past simple when a finished time is given
grammar: past simple with finished time expressions
examples: Have you ever tried sushi? Yes, I have. I tried it last summer.
She has never been to the sea.
